text: Gusevsky District (Russian: Гу́севский райо́н) is one of the fifteen administrative districts in Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia.[1] As a municipal division, it is incorporated as Gusevsky Urban Okrug, a status adopted on June 10, 2013.[5] Prior to that date, it was known as Gusevsky Municipal District, which consisted of one urban settlement and four rural settlements.[5] The district is located in the eastern part of the oblast and covers an area of 654.9 square kilometers (252.9 sq mi).[3] Its administrative center is the town of Gusev.[2] The population of the district was 37,142 in the 2010 census,[4] 37,461 in the 2002 census,[7] and 37,533 in the 1989 Soviet census.[8][9] The town of Gusev accounts for 76.1% of the district's total population.[4] The district is sparsely populated, with rivers such as the Pissa and the Angrapa flowing through it. The southern regions are primarily forested, while the northern areas feature a mix of forests and steppe pasture. The economy is primarily agricultural, and the main railway line and road connecting Kaliningrad to Moscow pass through the district.
